segments.text: What about you?

segments.text: Oh what do you study

segments.text: Language Okay And then I might play my guitar or watch something or waste time on my phone

segments.text: What do you, what's the most relaxing thing for you to wind down in the evenings?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I find playing my guitar very relaxing.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Why is that?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think because I have to concentrate and it's a different part of your brain that you use than the normal working brain.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How about you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I like watching TV to wind down, to feel relaxed.

segments.text: But like I said, recently I've been getting into doing jigsaw puzzles because I think similar to your guitar playing, it helps you to switch off your brain.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: you forget about the day you've just had at work

segments.text: Yeah

segments.text: and then something else

segments.text: and then something else?

segments.text: I try to limit my TV watching

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: something that I don't have to concentrate too hard because you know the

segments.text: OK. If I read a book, I fall asleep.

segments.text: Well, that's exactly why I do it.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: That's exactly why I do it. It helps me switch off.

segments.text: Or if I watch a film with subtitles and have to read the subtitles, that makes me fall asleep.

segments.text: So, Neil, I said I go to bed at nine. I usually go to sleep around 11. What about you?

segments.text: I go to bed later than that. I go to bed probably about 11. And I read, but then I fall asleep very quickly.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So we go to sleep at similar times, really.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes. I think if I didn't work or didn't have kids, I would stay up very late. I like staying up late. When I was a younger man, I stayed up very, very late.

segments.text: Interesting. I'm the opposite. My brain is dead in the evenings at night. I can't do anything late at night.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: The evening is the best part of the day

segments.text: I prefer the morning What about the weekend Is your evening routine different at the weekend

segments.speaker: Georgie

segments.text: so I also go to bed later and spend more of the night awake, I suppose.

segments.text: So you don't go to bed at nine at the weekends?

segments.text: Not usually. It depends, but mostly not.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap. We've had wind down, gradually relax after doing something stressful.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We heard stay up late, which means you continue staying awake late at night.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We heard night owl, who's someone who likes to stay up late in the evening.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And we had switch off, stop thinking about stressful things from your day.
